reviews.title: A deeply frustrating user experience to set it up
reviews.text:
I had this app on Android for years and it worked great. I recently switched to an iPhone and wanted to use it again but it asks SO many questions at setup and there’s no way to skip them. I literally just want an app that tells me salah times. 

I should have read the other reviews first before downloading, as it appears lots of people have the same frustrations but the developers either don’t read the feedback or don’t care. 

I got so annoyed by the 20th question that I deleted the app and didn’t bother with the rest of the setup. 

To the developers: I understand you’re trying to help people pray on time, but some of us don’t need an app. Just give us the option to skip all the unnecessary questions and look at the prayer times. 

I gave it 2 stars for the developers’ good intentions only. 

A deeply frustrating user experience that has put me off using it again

reviews.title: Loved it BUT had to request refund.
reviews.text:
This app is wonderfully designed and has very thoughtful touches/features. I feel like it’s the app I’ve waited years for….EXCEPT…
You can’t set a pre-reminder for Sunrise or Isha! How in the world?! For those of us who work a lot, this is major. I missed Maghrib a few times bc I was working and didn’t get the reminder. HUGE weird thing to omit, when it’s there for the other prayers. I emailed the developer several times with no response, even though the app is updated regularly. Fix this, and I’ll resubscribe in a heartbeat. 

Also, for the price, really should be a lifetime membership. Especially for a prayer specific app. But it is what it is. Just fix it.

reviews.title: Asks too many personal questions
reviews.text:
I recently got a new phone and had to reinstall the app. 

I was disappointed to find that it now forces you through a long series of highly personal questions before you can use it. These include asking how many times a day you pray and how you feel when you miss a prayer — questions that feel intrusive and completely unnecessary.

The app claims to be privacy-focused and ad-free, yet these questions come across as an attempt to collect sensitive personal and religious data. 

The questions are framed in a way that makes you feel guilty for not being a “good enough” believer. 

After forcing you through all these required questions, it uses that manufactured guilt to pressure you into paying for the premium version.

it uses that guilt to essentially say “you’re not good enough—now pay,” pressuring you into buying the premium version.

Collecting intimate religious data just to upsell is predatory. 

Feels more like emotional manipulation than a helpful tool.

That contradiction made me uncomfortable enough that I plan to delete the app entirely.

I hope the developers reconsider this approach. Users shouldn’t have to answer private questions about their faith and personal habits just to use a basic prayer app.

Once the developers remove these required questions—or make them truly optional with a large, clearly visible Skip button that isn’t hidden—I’ll happily revisit this review and update or remove it. Until then, I hope the developers listen to this feedback (and others

reviews.title: Pay-walled widget for quick hand prayer times
reviews.text: I used to love this app for being so minimalistic and seamless. arguably the most useful feature of the app, was being able to add a widget to your phone’s home page with the current prayer time and time remaining until the next one. With this feature, I was able to automatically get a reminder for prayer at a glance of my phone, which was the most useful feature which compelled me to stay true and complete all of my prayers since it’s a constant reminder. Now, this feature which was once free, is now locked behind a paywall forcing me to buy premium if I want to continue to use the most useful feature. For many of us, the problem with keeping our prayers is the constant reminder, the nudge in the right direction that we can’t blatantly ignore. If I was already so pious and dutiful in my prayers, I wouldn’t need an app, that I’d need to physically open, I’d already be aware of the timings intuitively. Now, you are assuming that most of your consumers just need to know the exact timing, which is far from the purpose of an app such as this, which is designed to help people become more disciplined, keep track of the prayers, and be held accountable gently. Now, as the app is, the onus is on me to voluntarily search for the app and open it 5 times a day. If I had such an intuitive affinity towards never missing a prayer in the first place, what’s the point of this app?

2. Idk if that’s a bug and the x was hidden but I had to tap random answers on so many screens just so it could try and sell me premium. 

Honestly, I 50% assume it must be a bug as I can’t imagine pillars becoming so user hostile.
